speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. To begin understanding your hand tremors and recent memory issues, can you tell me if these symptoms have been present continuously or if they come and go? Additionally, do you notice any stiffness or slowness in your movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease with possible co-existing Alzheimer's Disease or Dementia with Lewy Bodies. The combination of asymmetric resting tremor (worsening over a year), progressive functional impairment (reading difficulty), and recent episodic memory decline (paying bills) is highly suggestive. I will proceed with a clinical diagnosis based on this presentation, but if further confirmation via imaging is required for your records, I would request: REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.
